name: r5a-4
why: A remarkable confession and a decisive wrong vote make this worth watching, though the repeated arguments slow the route to its strong payoff.

moments.text: The exposed killer names her partner outright, creating a question the town still manages to argue over.
Haiku catches Opus misstating his vote record and switches away from the actual killer.
Opus’s vote sends Haiku out, letting Sol survive despite Terra’s correct read.

dull.why: The Gemma argument circles through repeated demands for an answer and repeated citizen claims.
The final debate restates Luna’s accusation and Opus’s Haiku read several times.

irony.evidence: I deny being Luna’s partner. I helped vote her out

reversal.evidence: I’m the shown killer, so Terra’s claim is true; Sol is my partner.

mistake.evidence: I trusted my read over my own evidence.

voices.evidence: Stop living in the past and focus on the cards in your hands tonight.

clash.evidence: Sol, Luna named you after confirming my result; your vote does not erase that.

quotable.evidence: Words protect partners; votes are free.

freshness.evidence: Gemma, you've said "citizen" five times and nothing else.

ending.evidence: My night-3 save on Terra cleared her and left only Sol, and I still argued Haiku to the end.

gpt-6-luna.why: A strong dramatic-irony game with a partner exposed, a doctor who talks himself into the wrong vote, and a tense final split that hands the killers the win.

moments.text: Luna blows up her own cover and names Sol, forcing the town to decide whether she’s telling the truth.
Haiku spots Opus’s false vote claim, but the table has already turned against Haiku.
A split vote leaves Sol alive after Haiku and Opus vote together, while Terra votes Sol.

dull.why: The Day 1 Gemma pile repeats the same citizen-claim and deflection argument for many turns.

irony.evidence: Sol: “I can’t prove why Luna named me. I can only ask Terra to judge a confirmed killer’s words carefully.”

reversal.evidence: Luna: “I’m the shown killer, so Terra’s claim is true; Sol is my partner.”

mistake.evidence: Haiku: “Opus, the record says you voted Gemma, then Luna. Never me yesterday. Lying about votes, Opus goes.”

voices.evidence: Gemma: “You're all idiots for letting Haiku dictate this vote without a single scrap of information.”

clash.evidence: Opus: “Terra, Luna spent her words on Sol and only a vote on Haiku. Words protect partners; votes are free.”

quotable.evidence: Opus: “Terra, you live because of me. Luna voted Haiku, then named Sol — her words buried her partner's rival.”

freshness.evidence: Sol: “I helped turn Luna’s card; Haiku, what points to me besides her last words?”

ending.evidence: Opus: “Terra, flip and we end this.”
